chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who was prevented from his wife, so he was not able to have intercourse with her, so he (peace be upon him) said:

If he is not able to have intercourse with other women besides her, then he should not keep her except with her agreement to that; and if he is able to have intercourse with other women, then there is no problem with keeping her.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for a man who cannot consummate marriage with his wife but can with others?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between general impotence and specific inability to consummate with one's own wife, ruling that if the man is capable of intercourse with others, he may retain his wife without her explicit consent to the limitation; however, if he is generally impotent, he must keep her only with her agreement. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the wife's right to sexual fulfillment (nafaqah al-jism) as a condition for the validity of keeping the marriage, reflecting the principle that marriage is not merely a contract but a fulfillment of mutual rights. The distinction underscores the practical application of 'rida' (consent) in mitigating the hardship of infertility or specific impotence within the marital bond.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddaq Bin Sadaqa, form Ammar Bin Musa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about a man who is seized from his wife, so he is not able upon going to her. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘

If it was such that he was not able upon going to other than her from the women, so he should not keep her except with her agreement with that; and if it was such that he was able upon other than her, so there is no problem with keeping her’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa who has said the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about the case of a man who is held back (by magic) and cannot go to bed with his wife. He (the Imam) said, ‘
If he cannot go to bed with other woman also, he must not keep her on hold without her consent; but if he is able to go to bed with other women then it is not unlawful to keep her.’”
